To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mass of the sneutrino can be determined to a precision of 0.2% for the first generation and 0.5-1% for the second and the third generation.

the mass of the sneutrino is most easily measured by examining the energy spectrum of the decay products of the selectron, and the precision is limited to about 1% by the uncertainty in the overall normalization of the cross section, rather than by the statistical precision of the data sample.

the precision with which sneutrino mass measurements can be performed depends on the sneutrino flavor, and is limited to about 0.2% for the electron flavor, 0.5-1.0% for the muon flavor, and about 5% for the tau flavor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of sneutrino masses at an e+ e- linear collider.
the study of the prospects of the measurement of the sneutrino masses in the context of the MSSM.
the determination of the sneutrino masses in the context of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the masses of the sneutrino partners of the first two generations of sleptons can be determined with precision comparable to that of the selectron masses, while those of the third generation can be determined only with a precision of 5% or worse, even at the 90 % C.L.
the mass of the lightest sneutrino can be extracted with 0.5-0.1% precision at the 90 CL, and the masses of the heavier ones with a precision of 5-2%.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mass measurements for sleptons and sneutinos at an e+ e- linear colliders are very challenging, especially when the masses of the sleptons are large.

the prospects for determining the masses of the second and third generations of sleptons and sneutrinos is not as promising as previously thought, but the prospects for determining m(\tilde{e}_R) and m(\nu_e) are still good.
the mass of the lightest sneutrino is measurable with an accuracy comparable to that of the selectron mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prospects for extracting sneutrino masses at an e+ e- linear collider are much more limited than has previously been thought.

the precision with which sneutrino masses can be extracted from a linear collider experiment is limited by the smallness of the production cross section, rather than the precision of the threshold scan.

the precision of the sneutrino masses that can be extracted at an e+ e- linear collider is significantly worse than the precision with which slepton masses can be extracted, even with the same integrated luminosity.
